scenes.title: Everything is moving
scenes.narration: A cricket ball, a train, a falling mango — kinematics describes how things move, without asking why.
bullets: Motion in a straight line and in a plane

scenes.title: The big ideas
scenes.narration: Tap each idea. Notice which ones have a direction — those are vectors.

nodes.label: Displacement
nodes.detail: Shortest straight-line change in position, with direction. Unit: metre (m).

nodes.label: Velocity
nodes.detail: Rate of change of displacement: v = Δx/Δt. It has direction.

nodes.label: Acceleration
nodes.detail: Rate of change of velocity: a = Δv/Δt. Unit: m/s².

nodes.label: Distance
nodes.detail: Total length of path travelled. Only size, no direction.

nodes.label: Speed
nodes.detail: Distance covered per unit time. Never negative.

scenes.title: Vector or scalar?
scenes.narration: Sort each quantity. Vectors need a direction; scalars need only a size.

scenes.title: First equation of motion
scenes.narration: Move the sliders. With constant acceleration, velocity grows in a straight line with time.

scenes.title: Anatomy of a projectile
scenes.narration: Tap each part of the ball's path to see what is happening there.
scenes.label: A ball kicked at an angle

parts.label: Launch
parts.detail: Velocity u at angle θ splits into uₓ = u cos θ (steady) and uᵧ = u sin θ (changing).

parts.label: Highest point
parts.detail: Vertical velocity is zero here; horizontal velocity is still u cos θ.

parts.label: Path shape
parts.detail: The path is a parabola because x grows steadily while y changes with t².

parts.label: Landing
parts.detail: Time of flight T = 2u sin θ / g when launch and landing are at the same height.

scenes.title: Range of a projectile
scenes.narration: Find the angle that sends the ball farthest. Then try two angles that add up to 90 degrees.
